On 8/2/26 11:03 AM, grace_oconnor wrote:
> Marcus — can you confirm the level of engineering effort for agent v3 testing?

Quick assessment: from a compatibility perspective agent v3 looks cleaner (modular kernel shim, better deferred-install path). Estimated integration testing timeline:
- Canary (2% fleet): 2 weeks
- Broader rollout (50%): additional 3 weeks with automated rollback policies
- Full fleet: 4–6 weeks (depends on user reboot cadence and patch windows)

Risk notes: there are a few older macOS images in our corp fleet that require a patched shim; we can handle that but will need a small hotfix from SentinelEdge for ~120 machines. That’s manageable within the migration window but means a hard cut by 12/31 if we want to avoid bridge licensing.

Recommendation: pursue migration now but secure a 3-month bridge license as contingency in case any surprise incompatibilities show up in the 50% rollout. From a cost perspective the migration delta is ~8% above current spend but reduces our long-term telemetry and support overhead.

Action items I propose:
- Olivia: please share a PO-ready two-line quote (migration vs bridge) and highlight the hotfix R&R for the mac images.
- Monica: negotiate a conditional credit if the hotfix support window slips beyond agreed SLA.
- David: estimate whether delayed migration changes our CapEx/OpEx treatment this fiscal quarter.

Marcus
Staff Engineer, Security — Redwood Inference
